knowledge:
- key_parameters: pseudoc=Pseudo count (hyperparameter) in a beta distribution for theta (default = 50; lower values increase reliance on observed data) ;; theta_init=Initial values of theta matrix representing P(E|FR) conditional probabilities (default = matrix(c(.99, .01, .3, .7), nrow=2)) ;; costs=List of candidate lambda values for finding the best L2 penalty hyperparameter via 10-fold cross-validation (default = c(100, 10, 1, .1, .01, 1e-3, 1e-4)) ;; verbose=Logical value to print parameter convergence updates at each EM iteration (default = FALSE)
- alternatives: GAM (Genomic Annotation Model)=A genomic-only model that uses genomic annotations alone (L2-regularized logistic regression) to predict variant effects. Prefer GAM when transcriptome/RNA-seq data is unavailable, but prefer RIVER when both WGS and RNA-seq data are available as it significantly improves predictive accuracy.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have paired personal genome (WGS) and transcriptome (RNA-seq) data and want to estimate the probability that rare genomic variants have a functional regulatory impact on nearby gene expression.
- pitfalls: Input file format requirements=The input compressed file must follow a strict column structure (Subject ID, Gene name, genomic features, Z-scores of gene expression, and N2pair column with integer IDs or NA) ;; N2 pairs assignment=If a subject has a unique set of rare variants, NA must be assigned in the N2pair column; otherwise, pairs sharing the same rare variants must have matching unique integer identifiers ;; EM convergence=The EM algorithm might terminate early or fail to converge if the tolerance threshold (1e-3) is not met, which can be monitored using verbose=TRUE.

workflows.name: river_evaluation
workflows.intent: Evaluate the predictive accuracy of the RIVER model compared to a genomic-only model (GAM) using held-out N2 pairs.
input: simulation_RIVER.gz (a gzipped text file containing subject ID, gene name, genomic features, expression Z-scores, and N2 pair identifiers)
workflows.stages: 1. Import experimental data using getData ;; 2. Run evaluation using evaRIVER with optional hyperparameters ;; 3. Extract and compare AUC values for GAM and RIVER
workflows.code:
filename <- system.file("extdata", "simulation_RIVER.gz", package="RIVER")
dataInput <- getData(filename)
evaROC <- evaRIVER(dataInput, pseudoc=50, theta_init=matrix(c(.99, .01, .3, .7), nrow=2), costs=c(100, 10, 1, .1, .01, 1e-3, 1e-4), verbose=TRUE)
cat('AUC (GAM-genomic annotation model) = ', round(evaROC$GAM_auc,3), '\n')
cat('AUC (RIVER) = ', round(evaROC$RIVER_auc,3), '\n')
cat('P-value ', format.pval(evaROC$pvalue, digits=2, eps=0.001), '***\n')

workflows.name: river_application
workflows.intent: Train the RIVER model on all instances and compute posterior probabilities of rare variants being functional for downstream prioritization.
input: simulation_RIVER.gz (a gzipped text file containing subject ID, gene name, genomic features, expression Z-scores, and N2 pair identifiers)
workflows.stages: 1. Import experimental data using getData ;; 2. Train and predict posterior probabilities using appRIVER ;; 3. Extract posterior probabilities for downstream analysis ;; 4. Plot the posterior probabilities using plotPosteriors
workflows.code:
filename <- system.file("extdata", "simulation_RIVER.gz", package="RIVER")
dataInput <- getData(filename)
postprobs <- appRIVER(dataInput, pseudoc=50, theta_init=matrix(c(.99, .01, .3, .7), nrow=2), costs=c(100, 10, 1, .1, .01, 1e-3, 1e-4), verbose=TRUE)
example_probs <- data.frame(Subject=postprobs$indiv_name, Gene=postprobs$gene_name, RIVERpp=postprobs$RIVER_posterior, GAMpp=postprobs$GAM_posterior)
head(example_probs)
plotPosteriors(postprobs, outliers=as.numeric(unlist(dataInput$Outlier))-1)
print(postprobs$fitRIVER$beta)
print(postprobs$fitRIVER$theta)
